Switzerland–United States Double Taxation Convention (effective 1998, amended by Protocol 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG; SR 955.0); Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (GwV; SR 955.01); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA; SR 955.033.0); Swiss Criminal Code arts. 305bis, 305ter and 260quinquies; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) arts. 697l–697o and arts. 951ff.; Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons and the Identification of Economic Beneficial Owners of 18 December 2020 (Transparency Act), in force as of 1 July 2024, with the associated Transparency Register implementing ordinances.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Swiss Notarized Deed of Incorporation comprising Articles of Association (Statuten), founders' declarations and subscribed share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss Notary Public in the canton of the registered seat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss notarial authentication (öffentliche Beurkundung); Hague Apostille not required for domestic registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Incumbency of each non-Swiss corporate shareholder or founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company or trade register in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention, or consular legalization if the issuing state is not a Hague Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and proof of residence for each ultimate beneficial owner and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss or foreign notary public, depending on residence; foreign notarizations require authentication
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the foreign notarial certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation of all foreign corporate constituent documents and identity documents into an official Swiss language (German, French or Italian)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss court-certified or sworn translator, foreign sworn translator subject to notarization and apostille where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the foreign translator/notary certificate or consular legalization for non-Hague states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and continuous screening of all founders, directors, shareholders, UBOs, business partners and customs counterparties against the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions lists and Swiss Embargo Act measures, EU consolidated financial sanctions to the extent relevant, and recognized PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence under GwG arts. 6 and 9 is required for politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and medium-risk customs brokerage structures; suspicious transaction reports must be filed with MROS via goAML.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex / Index central des raisons de commerce (www.zefix.ch), administered with the cantonal commercial register authorities (Handelsregisterämter) and the Swiss Federal Commercial Register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be true, clear, non-misleading and sufficiently distinctive under Swiss Code of Obligations art. 951. Names are recorded in Latin script; foreign-language names must be transliterated into Latin script and, where not in an official Swiss language, a German, French or Italian version must be available in the articles to avoid confusion. The legal-form suffix must be 'AG' for Aktiengesellschaft, 'SA' for Société anonyme/Società anonima, or 'AG/SA' as appropriate. Names that are purely descriptive, promotional, geographic-only, or capable of misleading as to the company's purpose, legal form or regulated status may be rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Eidgenossenschaft / Confederation / Confédération suisse / Confederazione Svizzera / Federal
Swiss / Schweiz / Suisse / Svizzera where the Swissness conditions under the Federal Act on the Protection of Trade Marks are not met
Bank / Banque / Banca / Sparkasse without FINMA banking authorisation
Insurance / Assurance / Versicherung / Assicurazione without the relevant insurance supervisory authorisation
Trust / Trustee / Treuhand / Fiduciary where such use implies financial intermediary or fiduciary licensing under Swiss financial market law
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must request a written negative ruling from the competent cantonal commercial register office. A written appeal may be filed within 30 days of service with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority, ordinarily the cantonal appeal court or designated administrative tribunal. Further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) in Saint Gallen/Bern, subject to the general procedural rules of the Federal Administrative Procedure Act. A fresh name reservation may be filed simultaneously to preserve priority during appeal proceedings.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered service address is permissible for the seat of a Swiss AG if a board member or a duly authorized person with signatory authority is reachable in Switzerland and all corporate records are available at the address. However, for a licensed customs brokerage house under the Swiss Customs Act (ZG/SR 631.0) and FOCBS supervision, a purely virtual office without verifiable operating presence is likely insufficient. A physical Swiss operating address or a demonstrable agent arrangement is expected for customs declarations, bonded transit records and AEO-type licensing. Virtual office arrangements therefore carry material substance risk for customs brokerage and should be supplemented by a real operational site or controlled licensed warehouse/agent facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated; estimated 35%–45% probability of an unannounced FOCBS or customs-authority inspection during the first 18 months after licensing, because the activity is classified ISIC 5229 and is subject to enhanced AML/CFT and customs supervision, with risk increasing further where non-resident UBOs or PEPs are identified.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association and foundation minutes (öffentliche Beurkundung)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Notary Public in the canton of seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal Notaries Fee Ordinance; notarial tariff based on planned share capital and charter complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for the Swiss Stock Company (AG/SA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official Swiss commercial register tariff; varies by canton and share capital structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, KYC/AML file preparation, PEP and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged Swiss law firm or compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Swiss Bar Association prevailing market benchmark for medium-risk corporate onboarding and due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, notarization, consular legalization and certified translation of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign authorities, apostille agencies, Swiss sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign official fees plus Swiss translator market rate of approximately CHF 80–150 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service address in the canton of seat for 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider or registered-office agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market benchmark in Switzerland for mail handling and registered service address

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: FOCBS customs broker authorization / AEO-style license application preparation and submission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal administrative fee schedule for customs authorization and professional diligence review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of AML/CFT internal regulations, customs compliance manual and client KYC procedures
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss compliance consultant or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a licensed, medium-risk customs brokerage house requiring documented AML/CFT and trade-control procedures

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, SR 220), Arts. 620-763 governing the Aktiengesellschaft (AG/SA), in particular Arts. 621 (minimum share capital), 628 (Sacheinlage / contribution in kind), 632 (paid-up capital), 643 (legal personality through registration), 718 (Swiss-resident board member), and 727a (opting out of the auditor); together with the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV, SR 221.411), Arts. 14 and 18-20.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / Greffe du registre du commerce du canton de Zoug), under the supervisory control of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA) within the Federal Office of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially authenticated Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), together with the electronic Application for Registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung im Handelsregister) filed pursuant to HRegV Art. 18.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Aktiengesellschaft must have a minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 (CO Art. 621); at least CHF 50,000 of the paid-up capital must be actually paid in before registration, subject also to the rule that no less than 20% of the nominal value of each share is paid (CO Art. 632). For cash contributions the paid-up amount must be deposited in a blocked escrow account opened at a Swiss bank in the name of the company in formation, and the bank must confirm in writing to the Commercial Register Office that the funds are at the free disposal of the Board of Directors; the account is released automatically upon registration. In-kind contributions (Sacheinlage) must be the subject of a special audit report under CO Art. 628 and must be described in the notarised deed of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: (1) The founders' report is approved and the subscription of one hundred registered shares of CHF 1,000 each, totalling the statutory minimum share capital of CHF 100,000, is ratified. (2) The Board confirms that the paid-up minimum of CHF 50,000 is deposited in a blocked account in the company's name and is at its free disposal upon registration. (3) The registered office is fixed at [street address], Canton of Zug, Switzerland, as stated in the Articles of Association. (4) The undersigned are appointed members of the Board of Directors, with [Name] as Chairman and [Name] as Company Secretary, each having accepted office. (5) The Chairman and Company Secretary, acting jointly, are authorised to sign the Commercial Register application and complete registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Bank Escrow and Paid-up Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (Bank in der Schweiz) operating a blocked escrow account for the company in formation; the bank's confirmation letter is addressed to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company under formation and deposit at least CHF 50,000 as paid-up capital; instruct the bank to issue the confirmation required by CO Art. 632 that the funds are at the free disposal of the Board of Directors. The original signed confirmation must be kept in the notary's file and appended to the registration application; the account is to be unblocked only upon entry in the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association containing the capital clause and corporate purpose (customs brokerage, freight forwarding, bonded transit management)
Lease or registered-office domiciliation agreement proving the Swiss seat address
Founders' identification documents and beneficial-owner (AML/GwG) disclosure file
Source-of-funds declaration and payment deposit order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML or source-of-funds evidence, promptly supplement the documentation or re-open the account at another licensed Swiss bank; alternatively, convert the cash contribution into a contribution in kind (Sacheinlage) evidenced by an auditor's special report under CO Art. 628 and recorded in the notarised deed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV) — VAT Main Department; eTax/eService customer portal (www.estv.admin.ch); central business register UID via ZEFIX.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign customs-brokerage entity without Swiss residence must apply through FTA eService using Form 'Registration of a legal entity / non-resident business', provide certified constitutional documents and appointment of fiscal representative if required, and obtain a Swiss UID/MWST-VAT number before invoicing taxable Swiss supplies. Registration is mandatory once the CHF 100,000 turnover threshold is met or for import transactions where VAT deferral is sought under a customs warehouse/bonded transit procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Swiss-resident AG; taxed on worldwide business profits at federal/cantonal/communal level; no pass-through eligibility; bonded transit facilities do not create income-tax-exempt-zone status).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections relevant to an AG: election to continue hidden reserves on transfer of assets or on migration of tax residence (Art. 61 DBG), group relief/consolidation upon qualifying intra-group transfer, partial taxation of qualifying dividend income, and anti-hybrid election/neutralization rules under Swiss implementation of BEPS (no elective pass-through is available).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable supplies (excluding VAT); foreign service providers must register when Swiss-scope services exceed CHF 100,000 per year; import VAT, customs duties and security are payable irrespective of this threshold, with bonded transit deferral available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance, government digital stamping, or continuous transaction control. Invoices must satisfy Art. 26 VAT Act content and retention requirements; electronic invoicing (QR-bill/eBill) is accepted. No taxpayer-facing clearance API is mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% Swiss VAT applies to exports of goods where the goods leave Switzerland and the exporter holds customs evidence of export; to services directly and verifiably connected with exported or transiting goods (including customs brokerage, handling and international freight); and to services supplied to a foreign-resident principal that benefit exclusively overseas. Eligibility requires a written contract, stated export nature, and contemporaneous documentary trail.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export declaration and export licence)
Bill of Lading (or equivalent Air Waybill / CMR international transport document)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of foreign-currency export proceeds receipt)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: FTA export audits require complete provenance and export documentation; missing or contradictory evidence leads to immediate reassessment at 8.1% plus 4.5% default interest and penalty taxes. Culpable false declarations are treated as VAT evasion: fines up to the tax evaded, imprisonment for serious cases, loss of input VAT deduction, and retrospective collection within the statutory limitation period (up to 10 years for evasion).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse) under the National Bank Act (NBG), with FINMA supervising financial intermediaries under the Banking Act (BkA) and Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility of CHF on both current and capital account; no exchange-control permit is required for foreign direct investment, capital injections, profit remittances, dividends, or repatriation of liquidation proceeds. A customs brokerage house may hold USD/EUR receivables and client duty funds without conversion mandates. The only material restrictions arise from AML/CFT due-diligence duties (GwG Art. 3-9), not from currency regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender, repatriation-timeline, or minimum-conversion-ratio rules for export receipts in Switzerland. Proceeds from customs brokerage fees or bonded-transit services may be retained indefinitely in any convertible currency, subject solely to Swiss accounting and tax documentation duties (OR Art. 957-963b) and to underlying customs-clearance evidence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency current account (CHF/EUR/USD) for fee collections and duty pass-through
Operational account plus segregated customs-security escrow (OR Art. 401 fiduciary) for BAZG bond cover
Treasury, FX and hedging account under ISDA for forwards and cross-currency swaps
Sub-account for branch-office collections at Swiss transit corridors
Domestic collection account for small-importer duty payments (SIC-only, low-cost)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-Low as primary rail. FINMA-licensed fintechs (BkA Art. 1b; public-deposit ceiling CHF 100m) may support low-value disbursements, but cannot issue customs guarantees, hold customs-duty settlements, or provide BAZG e-dec debit mandates. Offshore EMIs without FINMA authorisation are not viable as the sole treasury channel for a licensed customs broker; supplementary use is permissible under FINMA Circular 2016/07.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance of the UBO and an authorised signatory is the banking standard for a foreign-owned Medium-Risk Enhanced AG; remote video identification may be accepted only for low-risk roles (FINMA Circular 2016/07). At least one board member should attend the KYC interview in Zurich or Zug with certified statutes, the commercial-register extract, and the BAZG licence before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain or nominee arrangements on the Zug Commercial Register shareholding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified commercial register extract, notarised share register, GwG Art. 4 UBO declaration, SECO/FINMA sanctions-embargo screening, passport copies, source-of-wealth statement, and full shareholder organisational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified customs-broker licence and missing BAZG registration for ISIC 5229 operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FOCBS/BAZG registration or licence as customs representative (Zollgesetz Art. 97-101), professional-indemnity insurance certificate, and e-dec/NCTS access confirmation from the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous origin of equity for the AG capital increase (inbound shareholder injection)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-increase resolution, 12-month bank statements of the contributing shareholder, source-of-funds proof, deed of contribution, and updated Commercial Register excerpt showing post-increase share capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Web3 or crypto-wealth clients in Zug flowing through the brokerage account without declared purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client risk-rating documentation, declared customs transactions and e-dec records, no-cash policy, cryptocurrency origin declarations where relevant, and periodic monitoring reports satisfying GwG Art. 6-7 and FINMA AML ordinances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Volatile inbound-outbound flows not matching brokerage commissions and customs duty pass-through
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed brokerage mandates, invoices, duty assessment notices, NCTS transit messages, transport contracts, and a treasury policy segregating client duty funds from corporate operating funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's existing bank to the CH_AG account at UBS/ZKB, explicitly referencing the notarial deed and 'Kapitalerhöhung' in the remittance information; no SNB or FINMA authorisation required. The receiving bank requires the updated Commercial Register excerpt and shareholders' resolution. For injections above CHF 1m, an extended source-of-funds dossier must originate from the account-holding bank. Use ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPC' and ensure the originator's full legal name, address, account number, and value date are carried in MT103 field 50F for FINMA Circular 2016/07 traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct trade-supplier payments (INCOTERMS 2020) and client duty reimbursements; Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) via MT700/MT710 for high-value bonded-transit imports with deferred-duty guarantees; CHF domestic clearing via SIX SIC (SPS 2022 ISO 20022) including customer credit transfers; EUR corridors via euroSIC/TARGET2; customs duty and transit guarantee cash cover debited by BAZG through the e-dec/NCTS gateway against a segregated escrow account held at ZKB.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, EUR/USD) with UBS, ZKB, or Julius Bär under a bilateral ISDA 2002 Master Agreement; no SNB pre-approval required
European-style plain vanilla FX options for duty-price exposure on scheduled inbound shipments
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF) to align FX mismatch between brokerage fee receivables and customs-duty disbursements
NDFs permissible only for exotic corridor pairs (e.g., CHF/TRY-based transit trades) where the underlying currency is non-deliverable
Short-term CHF money-market deposits and reverse repos to bridge timing gaps between duty pre-funding, BAZG debits, and client reimbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Federal Direct Tax and Cantonal/Communal Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) acting for Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year-end; written extension normally available up to 12 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of approximately 4.25% p.a. on assessed tax; late-filing procedural fines of CHF 200–5,000; possible deemed assessment and administrative strike-off only after repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after end of the applicable VAT period (quarterly for most taxpayers; annual for taxpayers with taxable turnover ≤ CHF 2 million)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 4.5% p.a.; fines up to CHF 1,000 per reporting period for late filing; repeated failure may trigger VAT licence withdrawal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January following the calendar year for which wages were paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Declarant penalties up to 5% of unpaid contributions; default interest at 4.25%; failure to declare may result in provisional contribution assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Annexes to Tax Authorities (standard corporate secretarial duty)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office (under fiscal secrecy; no public commercial registry filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted together with the annual tax return, usually by 30 June for calendar-year companies (or within 6 months of reported year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Combined with tax return delinquency charges: default interest and administrative fines; negligent deficiency in statutory records may trigger special audit and additional tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by licence anniversary date; renewal application to be submitted before 1 December of the expiring year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal results in loss of authorised dealer status within the Swiss customs territory; operating without valid licence attracts administrative fines and potential suspension of customs clearance activities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit mandatory if any two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets > CHF 20 million; annual turnover > CHF 40 million; average annual headcount > 250 employees. In addition, listed companies, financial intermediaries, and licensed customs brokers with ancillary banking-like functions may be subject to ordinary audit irrespective of thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) and Swiss GAAP FER for statutory annual accounts; IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts or by company election.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Swiss law, no separate public UBO filing exists; however, the board must maintain an accurate Aktienbuch (share register) and provide an annual shareholder list in the tax return. Any share transfer during the year must be immediately registered. Custom brokers holding an AML licence must identify and periodically reaffirm beneficial ownership under the Anti-Money Laundering Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges and Usufructs on Shares

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000 - 35,000 for a typical customs brokerage AG, depending on transactional volume and consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% (Swiss federal statutory rate on profit after deduction of the direct federal tax itself; equivalent to 4.25% of pre-tax commercial profit; combined federal, cantonal and communal headline rates for an ordinary Zug-resident operating company generally range from 11.5% to 21.1%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No customs-brokerage-specific tax holiday or preferential federal deduction exists. Ordinary planning reliefs include the federal and cantonal participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, notional interest deduction on excess equity, cantonal patent/IP box for qualifying IP-linked software, and R&D super-deduction in certain cantons. Licensed customs brokerage commission income is ordinary taxable business income and does not qualify for patent-box treatment unless embedded in qualifying software developed in Switzerland.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal and cantonal income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Déclaration d'impôt pour personnes morales), filed electronically via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and the canton of Zug's approved electronic filing portal; the federal return is based on the ordinary Direct Federal Tax declaration integrated with the cantonal/tax-return package
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax period is the previous calendar or commercial fiscal year. The return must be filed within six months of issuance by the competent cantonal tax authority; for a 31 December year-end, cantonal practice generally requires lodgement by 30 June of the following tax year. Extended filing deadlines are available only with the tax authority's prior concession and do not suspend default interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial balance-sheet profit or loss per the statutory annual financial statements prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations, before corporate tax and before Swiss tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this line; the resident Swiss AG reports its worldwide commercial operating result, including customs brokerage commissions and transit-handling fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Foreign PE and Participation Exemption Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments excluding income attributable to foreign permanent establishments and qualifying participation dividends/capital gains under the participation exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE relief requires itemized foreign PE accounts and treaty-allocation schedules; non-resident parents cannot claim participation-exemption relief for the Swiss AG's underlying profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 - Non-Deductible Expenses and Hidden Distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions for non-business expenses, excessive director remuneration, unrealized value adjustments, and payments to related parties lacking economic justification; tax auditors will reclassify artificial customs-brokerage margins as hidden profit distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border invoices to related entities must be supported by a contemporaneous transfer pricing study and evidence of actual services rendered; unreported adjustments expose the non-resident owner to 35% Swiss withholding tax on deemed dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after application of the 7-year loss carryforward, participation exemption, own-capital interest relief, and any treaty-based PE exclusions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the Swiss AG cannot be consolidated with a foreign parent for Swiss direct federal tax because Switzerland has no full fiscal unity for corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct federal tax computed by applying the 8.5% statutory federal rate to the after-tax federal taxable profit, in accordance with the official federal corporate tax calculation schema
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The federal tax is borne solely by the Swiss AG; the non-resident shareholder obtains relief separately through the dividend withholding-tax refund procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing triggers procedural fines (Ordnungsbusse / amende pour l'ordre) under cantonal law of up to CHF 10,000 in serious cases, statutory default interest at approximately 4.0%-5.5% per annum on the unpaid federal tax, and a late-payment reminder surcharge; intentional non-filing or materially false filing can escalate into criminal tax evasion proceedings and a criminal fine of up to three times the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% (Verrechnungssteuer / impôt anticipé) withheld at source on dividend and profit-share distributions made by the Swiss AG to both resident and non-resident shareholders; relief is available only by treaty or qualified domestic-law refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief under a Swiss DTA is granted predominantly by refund rather than automatic at-source exemption. The non-resident shareholder must file a written refund application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) within the statutory limitation period, usually three years after the withholding date, attaching: (i) the official ESTV refund request form; (ii) the original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority for the relevant calendar year; (iii) a declaration of beneficial ownership; (iv) a custody or account statement evidencing the Swiss paying agent; and (v) a share register extract or equivalent proof of the applicable treaty-shareholding threshold, generally 10% for reduced participation-dividend rates. Where the DTA rate is zero, prior approval or a standing refund licence can be requested from ESTV for recurring dividend flows.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory Swiss withholding tax on IP licensing, software royalties, and customs-brokerage software licence payments; most Swiss DTAs also allocate exclusive taxation of royalties to the residence state, resulting in a 0% source rate. Interest: 35% statutory Swiss withholding tax applies only to interest on taxable Swiss bonds and money-market instruments; ordinary intercompany loan interest, bank deposits, and trade credit are not subject to Swiss source withholding. Under Swiss DTAs, treaty interest rates are typically 0% or a maximum source rate of 5-10%, depending on the counterparty jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Swiss administrative practice and the OECD TP framework adopted by the ESTV, a Local File-equivalent transfer pricing documentation set is expected where the Swiss customs-brokerage entity's annual controlled cross-border transactions exceed CHF 5,000,000 or where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds CHF 50,000,000; a Master File-style group documentation package is expected where consolidated worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 1,000,000,000. Even below these thresholds, the canton of Zug routinely requests contemporaneous pricing evidence for high-margin customs and logistics service arrangements.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) and imposes no annual ESR reporting obligation. Swiss law nevertheless enforces an economic-substance standard through case law, anti-abuse doctrines, and the Swiss withholding-tax beneficial-ownership rule. A customs-brokerage AG claiming treaty benefits must operate with locally employed licensed customs brokers, an actual Swiss office, locally taken business decisions, and segregated ERP/customs records. A letter-box company that merely books brokerage margin while foreign related parties perform all functions risks recharacterization as a sham or as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Direct Federal Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately or through gross negligence omitting brokerage commissions, customs-settlement rebates, transit-handling revenue, or foreign intermediary invoices from the Swiss corporate tax return; using false customs declarations to underreport taxable income; falsifying statutory audit files to conceal hidden profit distributions to the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud and aggravated omission of income are sanctioned under Articles 175 and 186 of the Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act with imprisonment or monetary penalties, and the amount of the fine may reach up to three times the tax evaded in serious cases. The tax administration may also re-open the final assessment for up to ten years and impose default interest. False customs declarations under the Swiss Customs Act may trigger confiscation of assets and fines up to CHF 2,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Swiss administrative criminal law, the directing manager, chief executive officer, and licensed customs broker are personally liable where the tax offence is committed in a corporate capacity and cannot be effectively assigned to a natural person. Courts may pierce the corporate veil under Articles 144 and 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, ordering the responsible director to restitute the evaded tax and related withholding tax. Travel bans, asset freezes, professional disqualification, and custodial sentences of up to five years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mis-Pricing and Constructive Dividend
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length fees for customs-brokerage services, logistics mark-ups, management fees, or shareholder-loan interest in order to shift Swiss taxable profit to a foreign affiliate; invoicing for services that were never performed; unilateral year-end recalculation of transfer prices without corresponding adjustment documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss tax authority reclassifies the excess amount as a hidden profit distribution (verdeckte Gewinnausschüttung), denies the expense deduction for Swiss tax purposes, increases taxable profit, and imposes 35% Swiss withholding tax on the deemed distribution, with default interest at approximately 5% per annum. Treaty reduction of the withholding tax is disallowed if the TRC, beneficial-ownership declaration, or contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is deficient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the mispriced invoices are jointly and severally liable under Swiss withholding-tax law if the company fails to remit the tax on the deemed distribution. The CFO or managing director can be prosecuted as an accessory to tax evasion and ordered to compensate the full tax shortfall. Corporate relief or indemnification does not exclude individual criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Letter-Box Entity Lacking Economic Substance and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Swiss AG registered in Zug with no licensed customs staff, no operational Swiss office, no locally managed customs filings, board meetings held exclusively abroad, and all core brokerage functions subcontracted to the foreign parent, while the Swiss entity claims DTA benefits and low-canton tax treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority disregards the Swiss entity for tax purposes and reallocates profits to the foreign principal under the substance-over-form and anti-abuse rules; treaty benefits are denied under the principal-purpose test. A 35% withholding tax is assessed on undeclared profit-shifting plus default interest, and the commercial register may strike the company for non-complying registered seat requirements under Article 12 of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominal Swiss director who certifies false substance evidence faces criminal liability for falsifying documents and assisting tax evasion, removal by the commercial registry, a five-year ban on serving as a director, civil restitution claims for the full tax shortfall, and personal enforcement measures including travel bans and asset freezing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Violations in Customs-Brokerage Payment Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving untraceable cash as purported customs prepayments, executing cross-border wire transfers without identifying the beneficial owner, handling third-party refunds through the collective customs broker ACH interface without required know-your-customer verification, or using the customs-brokerage account to layer proceeds for unlicensed crypto or offshore payment providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory enforcement may include FINMA administrative orders, monetary sanctions, asset confiscation, and revocation of the Swiss customs brokerage licence under the Swiss Customs Act. Criminal prosecution under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act and Swiss Criminal Code may lead to custodial sentences of up to five years, fines, and permanent exclusion from regulated financial and customs intermediation activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers, licensed customs brokers, and board members can be prosecuted in their individual capacity because corporate limited liability does not shield wilful AML misconduct. Directors face criminal fines, imprisonment, civil damages for client losses, withdrawal of their personal brokerage licence, travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification from the board of any Swiss regulated entity.
